headline: Welcome to the live coverage of stage 11 of La Vuelta 26
subtext: Another opportunity for the sprinters? Today’s route between Cartagena and Lorca (153.8 km) is essentially flat (1,350 metres of elevation gain) but the Alto de Aledo (9.5 km at 4.2 %) offers an opportunity to flip the script just before the final 30 kilometres. The neutral start is set at 13:50, the start proper at 14:05 after a 6.4 km parade, and the winners should be crowned at around 17:30.

headline: Pedersen won’t start stage 11
subtext: “After battling illness over the past few days, Mads will now focus on making a full recovery before turning his attention to his remaining targets this season”, Lidl-Trek announced this morning. The Danish star was second in Xeraco (stage 8) and 4th in Manosque (stage 2). He had won stages and the green jersey in his two previous La Vuelta participations (2022, 2025).

headline: Cycling history in Cartagena
subtext: Cartagena has been a stage town in three previous editions of La Vuelta: 1962, 1976 and 2023.On the last occasion, the race headed to Collado de la Cruz de Caravaca (stage 9). Breakaway rider Lennard Kämna won the stage and Sepp Kuss retained La Roja. Cartagena is a classic venue of the Vuelta a Murcia, recently witnessing the victories of Alessandro Covi (2022) and Ben Turner (2023). Cartagena was home to Spain’s 2023 Junior championships. Markel Beloki won the time trial. Cartagena also gave rise to the Saura dynasty. Born there in 1901, José Saura was Spain’s national champion in 1922 and 1926. His three sons - Gabriel, Jesus and José - were cyclists. After he retired, Gabriel Saura managed Spain’s national selection as well as professional teams.

headline: Local heroes
subtext: Lorca is the hometown of Juan Zurano, the first rider from Murcia to win a stage of La Vuelta, in 1973. He turned 78 yesterday. The most famous rider from Murcia is Alejandro Valverde, whose list of achievements includes the overall victory at La Vuelta 2006. He won 12 stages in the Spanish Grand Tour, stood seven times on the overall podium (a record) and won 4 times the points standings (a shared record).Valverde won the 2019 national champion title in Murcia. The race started in Los Alcazares (km 36.2 on today’s route). Among the most notable riders from Murcia, José Joaquin Rojas is in La Vuelta 26 as a sports director for Movistar. José Luis Faura (Burgos Burpellet BH) is the local rider today. He hails from Pliego, around 50 kilometres north of Lorca.

headline: Birthday boy(s)
subtext: Sente Sentjens (Alpecin-Premier Tech) turns 21 years old today. The Belgian youngster is taking part in his first Grand Tour. Today is also Tom Steels’ 55th birthday. The winner of two stages in La Vuelta 1996, he is in the event this year as a sports director for Soudal Quick-Step.

headline: Let’s roll
subtext: The peloton make their way to the start proper with a 6.4 km parade.

headline: La Roja
subtext: Enric Mas (Movistar) rode at the front of the peloton yesterday as attackers tried to turn the race upside down. He is the first Spanish rider to hold La Roja for at least three days since Alberto Contador won the 2014 edition. Mas leads the overall standings with a gap of 1’18’’ to Primoz Roglic (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) and 1’39’’ to Felix Gall (Decathlon CMA CGM). Oscar Onley (Netcompany Ineos) is fourth, trailing by 2’20’’.

headline: Green jersey
subtext: Still chasing his first stage winches year, Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) had to settle for the fourth place yesterday in Elche de la Sierra, but he retained the lead of the points standings with a tally of 143 points. In his wake (5th), Alessandro Romele (XDS Astana) moved up to the second position with 76 points. Matthew Brennan, Van Aert’s teammates, follows with 67 points.

headline: Polka dot jersey
subtext: Yesterday’s hills brought no change at the top of the mountains standings - Santiago Buitrago (Bahrain Victorious) has 29 points, five more than Enric Mas (Movistar). Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility) follows with 19 points.

headline: White jersey
subtext: Oscar Onley (Netcompany Ineos) is still 5’45’’ ahead of Jakob Omrzel (Bahrain Victorious), while Jarno Widar (Lotto Intermarché) trails by 7’14’’.

headline: Team standings
subtext: With Alessandro Romele (5th), Yevegeniy Fedorov (12th) and Henok Mulubrhan (15th) in the mix yesterday, XDS Astana had the best collective performance in Elche de la Sierra, but Decathlon CMA CGM retained the lead of the overall team standings ahead of Netcompany Ineos (42’’55’’) and Visma-Lease a Bike (50’12’’).

headline: Combativity award
subtext: Michael Gogl (Alpecin-Premier Tech) will race with a distinctive bib today as he was named the most combative rider en route to Elche de la Sierra.

headline: Stage 11 is ON!
subtext: There are 166 riders int he peloton in the absence of Mads Pedersen (Lidl-Trek).

headline: 3 riders on the move: Hayter, De la Cruz, Novak
subtext: Domen Novak (UAE Emirates XRG), David de la Cruz (Pinarello Q36.5) and Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step) lead the way. Siuhé Fernandez (Burgos Burpellet BH) is in pursuit.

headline: The break is gone?
subtext: At km 4, Fernandez trails by 12'' while the gap to the peloton is up to 1'05''.

headline: 4 leaders: Hayter, Covi Novak, Fernandez
subtext: Alessandro Covi (Jayco AlUla) was up there instead of David de la Cruz (Pinarello Q36.5). Sinuhé Fernandez (Burgos Burpellet BH) has bridged the gap. The peloton trail by 1'20''.

headline: Not much margin for the attackers?
subtext: So far, the gap is controlled at 1'10''.

headline: A usual suspect at the front
subtext: Sinuhé Fernandez (Burgos Burpellet BH) has made today’s breakaway after already spending days 2, 8 and 10 at the front. He received the combativity award after he was the sole attacker on stage 8.

headline: Should we also have expected Covi’s attack?
subtext: At 27 years old, the Italian is a seasoned baroudeur. And he’s found success in the area: in 2022, he won the Vuelta a Murcia in Catagena. It was his first professional victory and it significantly marked him: “I have a tattoo of an anchor because the finish was at the port”, he said at the start.

headline: Visma | Lease a Bike leading the peloton
A minute and a half
subtext: Thirty kilometres into the stage, the peloton maintain a tight leash on the breakaway.

headline: Visma-Lease a Bike and Cofidis pull the bunch
subtext: The same two teams already controlled yesterday's stage, but they could'nt claim the win in Elche de la Sierra. They want another shot in Lorca.

headline: 3 WorldTeams have yet to win a Grand Tour stage this year
subtext: After the recent victories of Movistar (Enric Mas at Alto de Aitana, stage 9) and Groupama-FDJ United (Bastien Tronchon in Elche de la Sierra, stage 10), three World Teams have yet to win a Grand Tour stage this year: Lotto Intermarché, Picnic PostNL, and NSN. Cofidis is the only Pro Team with a Grand Tour victory (Bryan Coquard in Xeraco, stage 8).

headline: The sprinters’ teams are keeping the breakaway under control
Van Aert yesterday, Brennan today?
subtext: Matthew Brennan spoke about Visma-Lease a Bike's plans today at the start: “Yes [the plan was to sprint with Wout van Aert yesterday and me today]. He was pretty keen to go for yesterday. The course I would say suited him quite nicely as well, so that was the plan that we went with. I think [today’s course] suits me nicely. It’s a sprint day, so we can give it a try; and with the guys we have it can really work out nicely.” Do you want your team to be first into the final corner? “Absolutely. It’ll be everyone’s goal to be there in the final corner. It’s gonna be hectic. It’s big wide roads. We just have to try our best.”

headline: A gap of 1'40'' at km 40
subtext: That's the biggest gap so far today.

headline: 43.7 km in the first hour
subtext: Correction: the gap at km 40 was 1'14''. And now it has dropped to 50''.

headline: 50 kilometres into the stage
subtext: Domen Novak (UAE Emirates XRG), Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step), Alessandro Covi (Jayco AlUla) and Sinuhé Fernandez (Burgos Burpellet BH) work well at the front. But the peloton want to stay close: 42 seconds.

headline: The gap stabilises again
subtext: But it's only up to 40 seconds.

headline: The peloton accelerate through the wind
subtext: Bahrain Victorious, Tudor and XDS Astana want to split the bunchwith 93 km to go.

headline: The attackers are caught with 90 km to go
subtext: Stefan Küng (Tudor) takes a strong turn at the front of the peloton and then it's EF Education-EasyPost setting the pace. Around 30 riders are off the back.

headline: 2 pelotons battle
subtext: Hugo Hofstetter (NSN) is among the riders in the second group, half a minute behind the leaders with 85 km to go.

headline: Back together
subtext: As the calm returns in the first bunch, the stragglers brdige the gap with just over 80 kilometres remaining.

headline: Halfway through the stage
subtext: The situation settles again, with Cofidis and Visma-Lease a Bike back at the front of the peloton.

headline: Hayter goes again
subtext: Part of the first breakaway, Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step) participates in a new 2-man move with Larry Warbasse (Tudor). They attacked 74km from the finish.

headline: 30 seconds
subtext: Hayter and Warbasse enter the final 70 kilometres.

headline: Cycling memories from Lorca
subtext: Lorca is a stage finish for the fourth time in La Vuelta. The winners in Lorca are Italy’s Umberto Drei (1950), Belgium’s Jean Ronsmans (1970), and the USA’s Tyler Farrar (2010). The latter got the better of Koldo Fernandez and Mark Cavendish to take his fourth Grand Tour stage win (the 5th and final would come at the end of La Vuelta, in Madrid). Philippe Gilbert was wearing La Roja, the new overall leader’s jersey introduced that year. Lorca has hosted La Vuelta stage starts in 1950, 1970 and 2017. On the last occasion, the race headed to Calar Alto, where tomorrow’s stage finishes.In 2015, Xabier Mikel Azparren (ITT) and Ivan Cobo (road race) dominated Spain’s U17 national championships in Lorca. Lorca also took part in Spain’s 2019 national championships, hosting the finish of the women’s race (won by Lourdes Oyarbide) and the men U23 (Carmelo Urbano).Lorca has also been visited by local events, notably the Vuelta a Murcia.

headline: The average speed after 2 hours: 46.3 km/h
subtext: It's been a very fast day through the wind.

headline: Today’s the day for a sprint
Faura: "Let’s hope we can make our presence felt a bit"
subtext: José Luis Faura (Burgos Burpellet BH) is the local rider today, hailing from Pliego, around 50 kilometres north of Lorca: "I’m really pleased to be able to race here, in front of my home crowd and everyone who supports me, on familiar roads. Let’s hope we can make our presence felt a bit. It’s not a very tough route, to be honest. Ultimately, the 1,000-metre climb over 150 kilometres is mainly because we’re starting from the coast and, as they say, we’re heading slightly inland, gradually climbing, with the Santa pass about 30 kilometres from the finish. I think it’s clear today is a day for sprinters. We’ll try to make our presence felt in the breakaway, and we’ve also got an ace up our sleeve in César Macías, who can do very well."

headline: Still 30 seconds
subtext: The gap decreased to 15 seconds but it's back up to 32 seconds as Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step) and Larry Warbasse (Tudor) enter the final 50 kilometres.

headline: Kamna: "I'm back to my full capacity"
subtext: Lennard Kamna (Lidl-Trek) won the Cartagena > Collado de la Cruz de Caravaca stage in 2023: "It's a special moment for me; or a special place. I think I'm back to my full capacity. Right now, I'm still not like 100% perfectly in shape, but I'm still capable of getting there and I'm really happy to be at a Grand Tour, because three years ago was my last Grand Tour. I'm really happy to be here and to get these races in the legs. My personal hopes are that I get better day by day and that I can maybe be in a breakaway in the next couple of days. Just in general, I hope the best for our team, that we finish it off with scale and that we are in a really good GC position."

headline: Hayter leads the way at the intermediate sprint; 15 points for Van Aert
subtext: Immediately after the sprint, the road rises up the Alto de Aledo (9.5km at 4.2%).

headline: Results of the itnermediate sprint (Totana, km 111.9)
subtext: 1. Hayter, 20 pts / 6'' 2. Warbasse, 17 pts / 4'' 3. Van Aert, 15 pts / 2'' 4. Coquard, 13 pts 5. Romele, 10 pts

headline: Vermaerke and McKenzie hit the deck
subtext: Kevin Vermaerke (UAE Emirates XRG) rapidly gets back up. Hamish McKenzie (Jayco AlUla) appears to be more affected by the crash.

headline: The attackers are caught on the final climb
subtext: Pinarello Q36.5 up the pace.

headline: Dunbar sets a very strong pace
subtext: Van Aert is on his wheel. Many riders are dropped with a bit more than a kilometre of ascent left.

headline: Van Aert sprints to the summit
subtext: Buitrago is second.

headline: Results at Alto de Aledo (cat. 3, km 121.8)
subtext: 1. Van Aert, 3 pts 2. Buitrago, 2 pts 3. Fortunato, 1 pt

headline: Visma-Lease a Bike drive a reduced bunch into the final 25 kilometres
subtext: A couple of riders tried to attack but Bruno Armirail (Visma-Lease a Bike) covered their move. There's a small group with Joao Almeida, Ivo Oliveira (UAE Emirates XRG), Jakob Omrzel (Bahrain Victorious) and Alberto Dainese (Soudal Quick-Step) not far behind.

headline: 3 teams to drive the peloton
subtext: Pinarello Q36.5 and Uno-X Mobility collaborate with Visma-Lease a Bike.

headline: The average speed after 3 hours: 45.9 km/h
subtext: The riders are about to enter the final 15 kilometres.

headline: The final 10 kilometres
subtext: Visma-Lease a Bike and Kern Pharma increase the pace.

headline: Wout van Aert (Visma | Lease a Bike)
Netcompany Ineos drive the bunch
subtext: The British team has lost Ben Turner but they can count on Axel Laurance.

headline: 5 kilometres to go
subtext: Visma-Lease a Bike are back at the helm with Armirail, Laporte, Van Aert and then Brennan.

headline: Uno-X Mobility move up
subtext: Magnus Cort is in fourth position with 2 km remaining.

headline: Last kilometre
subtext: It's a hard battle for the front positions!

headline: Matthew Brennan wins stage 11 of La Vuelta 26!
subtext: Already his third stage win in his first Grand Tour!

headline: Top 5
subtext: 1. Matthew Brennan (Visma-Lease a Bike) 2. Bryan Coquard (Cofidis) 3. Jordi Meeus (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) 4. Magnus Cort (Uno-X Mobility) 5. Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike)
